author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Canonical record for Claudia Bush Letters, PKD's letter. Linked to a single archive manifestation preserved in the archive.
page_summary:
Claudia Bush Letters is the canonical works-table record for PKD's letter corpus item. The record links the archive's preserved manifestation of the work to the broader corpus and gives researchers a single place to follow its bibliographic and interpretive context.

The preserved archive item here is Claudia Bush Letters (1975-1979).

The source record itself summarizes the work as follows: The Claudia Bush letters form one of the richest interpretive correspondences in the Selected Letters. Bush wrote seriously about Dick's work, and Dick used the exchange to test explanations of Ubik, Flow My Tears, The Man in the High Castle, The Lathe of Heaven, Zebra, the right hemisphere, the 1971 break-in, and his post-2-3-74 religious model. The corpus is valuable because it shows Dick writing to a knowledgeable reader who was neither merely a fan nor merely an editor: he is often reflective, argumentative, speculative, and autobiographical in the same letter.

Current segmentation finds 27 Claudia Bush/Bush Krenz letters from January 1975 through March 1979. This document should be treated as a corpus wrapper; individual high-value letters can still receive their own document records when they become focal evidence.

The entry is most useful when tracing publication context, later commentary, or relationships to other works.
